_comment: Hand-maintained, not fetched hourly. Receiving-government cash incentives on inward remittances - a different thing from provider markup, paid separately (often days later) and only to eligible transfers. Only include a corridor here if you can confirm it's ACTIVE from a central bank or major provider source, with the source URL and the date you checked. Researched 2026-09-19: of the 16 corridors this site tracks, only Bangladesh has a confirmed-active scheme. Pakistan's incentive schemes (TTCIS, SDRP) were ended by the State Bank of Pakistan on 2026-07-01; a replacement was announced as 'coming soon' in August 2026 but was not live as of this research. Nigeria's 'Naira 4 Dollar' rebate structure was disrupted by a CBN mandate (effective 2026-05-01) requiring all payouts in naira only, and its status under that regime could not be confirmed. Sri Lanka's per-dollar incentive was confirmed discontinued (ended 2022). Egypt, Philippines, Nepal: no government incentive scheme found (only infrastructure initiatives). India: LRS/RDA are outbound-remittance rules, not an inbound incentive. Vietnam: only bank-specific promotional campaigns exist (Agribank/Western Union, MSB), not a government policy - excluded on the same principle CLAUDE.md's gap #2 already applies to promo rates distorting rankings.

BDT.eligibility: Wage earners' remittances sent through a legal/formal channel only (bank deposit or mobile wallet such as bKash or Nagad). Does NOT cover freelancing, IT/remote-job income, gifts, FDI, or trade payments.
BDT.documentation: None required for transfers under BDT 500,000. Above that threshold, the recipient has 5 days to provide supporting documentation.
BDT.notes: Introduced at 2% in 2019 by the Government of Bangladesh; raised to 2.5% in January 2022. Paid by the Bangladeshi government, not the transfer provider - typically credited separately and can land days after the transfer itself, not at the same time. Corroborated by five independent providers describing the same program consistently (Western Union, WorldRemit, Ria, TapTapSend, RemitChoice) plus Mutual Trust Bank, a Bangladeshi bank rather than a sender-side provider, and by The Financial Express (Dhaka) reporting the same 2.5%/January 2022 figures from the Finance Minister's budget speech. The underlying Bangladesh Bank circular (referenced by secondary sources as 'FE Circular Letter No. 01' of 2 January 2022) was NOT located directly: bb.org.bd's own remittance data page does not mention the incentive despite a search-engine summary claiming otherwise, one guessed circular-letter URL on bb.org.bd 404'd, and a downloaded PDF for a similarly-named circular ('FE Circular No. 01' of 6 January 2022) turned out to be an unrelated notice about trade-transaction extensions. Re-attempted 2026-09-20 at the requester's request; still unresolved. Treat as provider-sourced, not primary-sourced, until the actual BB circular is found.
